assessment.reason: The model edge is modest but survives its own sensitivity floor at +275, and settlement follows published rules. The cushion is thin and only one book prices this exact line. No specific unresolved fact clearly overturns the case.
assessment.model_case: The projection of about 0.36 assists on 16.8 minutes implies roughly one assist every three games. That is plausible for a middle-six role. assessment.price_case: This is the main 0.5 line at +275, with break-even near 11-to-4 against. The model's minimum is about +271, so a small price drift erases the case. A single other book is not broad consensus.
assessment.context_case: The injury table only partially supports the goalie assumption, and Minnesota's defensive absences are context, not proof. Protas does not appear in the excerpt, but that does not establish his health.

qualitative_review.countercase: The edge rests on a small model-versus-market gap at long odds from an unvalidated, experimental model. Protas's line and power-play usage are unconfirmed. Any price move toward +270 or shorter removes the margin entirely.

findings.note: NHL.com's game-day projected lineup has Aliaksei Protas in the lineup on the second line with Pierre-Luc Dubois and Tom Wilson, and does not list him as injured. Minnesota is missing Brock Faber, Jared Spurgeon, both Folignos and Gustavsson.

ESPN's Capitals line chart is about nine days old. It lists Protas on the third line with Dubois and Wilson, puts him on the second penalty-kill unit and leaves him off both power-play units, which limits his chances to pick up assists.

The Capitals' CapsToday page links to a District Standard story headlined 'Goals Will Come: Aliaksei Protas Searching to Find His Game,' which points to an early-season scoring slump. The date of that story is unclear.

Konecny has missed 10 games with a lower-body injury, and his return was not confirmed. He practiced fully on Friday and Saturday, and coach Tocchet said only that he could be an option to play Sunday, though the projected lineup has him on the top line with Zegras and Dvorak.

The Flyers are 3-8-3-1, and their recent games have mostly gone under the total, including 6-0-1 to the under in their last seven home games against strong road teams. The page lists no expert or computer picks for this game.
Before his injury, Konecny had 3 assists in 5 games this season (1 on the power play), averaging 16:48 of ice time. His ESPN status still shows IR from his placement about 20 days ago.
